description: The Execution System for IIT Kanpur's Bachelor of Cybersecurity — turn your current academic and technical situation into a clear, personalized execution path.
outcome: Turn your current academic and technical situation into a clear, personalized execution path for IIT Kanpur B.Cyber and technical authority

modules.title: Know the Truth & Selection Reality
modules.description: Understand the exact criteria of IIT Kanpur's B.Cyber program, separate JEE myths from screening reality, and see the 2026 vs 2027 shifts.
outcome: Demystify JEE Main cutoff myths vs the actual screening filter
Understand the role of the C3iHub & WSAIS admission committee
Learn why 90% of file uploads get ignored and what stands out
Know the format and failure traps of the on-campus hackathon

steps.title: The JEE Main Baseline Truth
steps.description: Understand that JEE Main is a qualification gatepass, not a ranking contest for this program.
steps.details: IIT Kanpur designed B.Cyber in collaboration with IIT Madras to find students with genuine technical aptitude, not just PCM exam stamina. JEE Main serves as an eligibility screening baseline to ensure basic mathematical foundation. A 99 percentile without proof-of-work will be rejected over an 88 percentile with genuine Linux curiosity and public problem-solving.

steps.title: The 'Evidence of Prior Work' Evaluation
steps.description: Learn what the committee actually evaluates when reviewing uploaded application files.
steps.details: The application portal requests evidence of prior work or technical exposure. The fatal mistake applicants make is uploading flat resumes, course completion certificates from Coursera/Udemy, or school HTML projects. The committee looks for verifiability: active GitHub commits, OverTheWire Bandit problem-solving notes, TryHackMe badges, or creative proof-of-work like a 2-minute unlisted video walkthrough.

steps.title: The On-Campus Hackathon Ground Reality
steps.description: Prepare for the controlled laboratory environment inside IIT Kanpur.
steps.details: Shortlisted candidates are invited to IIT Kanpur for an in-person assessment. The hackathon is Jeopardy-style CTF across Linux, Networking, Web, and Cryptography. Most candidates fail not because they lacked knowledge, but due to poor triage: wasting 90 minutes down a rabbit hole for a 50-point problem instead of capturing the 300 points of accessible foundational flags.

steps.title: The 2027 Admission Evolution
steps.description: Anticipate the transition from JEE Main screening to an Aptitude Test + Hackathon model.
steps.details: Reports and admissions trends indicate a formal dedicated entrance assessment covering mathematical ability, discrete logic, and cybersecurity aptitude, followed directly by the on-campus practical hackathon. Preparing hands-on problem-solving skills today ensures full readiness regardless of testing format changes.

prompts.title: Current Standing Self-Diagnostic
prompts.text: Review your current profile against the three IITK screening pillars: (1) Academic baseline (JEE Main/Aptitude standing), (2) Verifiable proof-of-work (GitHub/CTF assets), (3) Practical debugging stamina. Identify which of these three pillars is currently at 0% and requires immediate focus.

steps.title: Classify Your Academic Profile
steps.description: Select whether you are managing high school JEE pressure or college reset anxiety.
steps.details: Profile A: Class 12 / Dropper student. Your top risk is getting distracted by cyber and tanking your JEE Main cutoff score. Profile B: 1st Year College student (e.g. RGIPT, tier-2/3) seeking skills and placement redemption. Profile C: 2nd/3rd Year student seeking an immediate IIT research internship (Jan/Summer) as well as B.Cyber transition.

steps.title: Audit Your Technical Baseline
steps.description: Be brutally honest about what you can execute in a terminal right now.
steps.details: Baseline 1: Total Zero — have never used Linux or written a program. Baseline 2: C / Mathematics — understand loops, logic, and math puzzles (e.g. IOQM/RMO background), but zero security exposure. Baseline 3: Python / Scripting — can write simple scripts, know basics of web/data. Baseline 4: Web / Tool dabbler — comfortable with HTML/JS and basic networking.

steps.title: Set Your Weekly Time Constraint
steps.description: Define realistic hours that won't collapse during exam weeks.
steps.details: Option 1: 3–5 hours/week (Weekend Sprint). Strictly for Class 12 JEE students or intensive semester periods. Option 2: 8–10 hours/week (Balanced Rhythm). 1 hour daily + 3 hours on weekends. Option 3: 15+ hours/week (Intensive Transition). For gap students or light semester schedules.

steps.title: Calculate Your Primary Gap
steps.description: Pinpoint the single fatal bottleneck in your current setup.
steps.details: If Profile A: Your gap is a structured 2-hour weekend routine that builds proof-of-work without stealing focus from Physics/Chemistry/Maths. If Profile B with C/Maths: Your gap is converting theoretical code into Linux terminal competence and public GitHub writeups. If Profile C: Your gap is direct faculty-aligned research output.

I can sustainably dedicate [5 / 10 / 15] hours per week without compromising my primary exams. My biggest obstacle today is [lack of direction / fear of JEE damage / zero public evidence].'

Clear weekly milestone targets with tangible definitions of done

steps.title: Activate Pathway-Alpha: The JEE Protection Track
steps.description: For 11th/12th/Dropper aspirants dedicating 3–5 hours per week.
steps.details: 85% of your mental energy remains on JEE Main preparation (Physics, Chemistry, Maths). Security work is strictly confined to a Saturday/Sunday 2-hour window. Weeks 1–3: OverTheWire Bandit 1–10. Weeks 4–6: Basic Wireshark inspection of 3 sample PCAP files. Weeks 7–9: 10 beginner challenges on PicoCTF. Weeks 10–12: Create your GitHub learning repository and document your notes.

steps.title: Activate Pathway-Beta: The College C & Systems Track
steps.description: For 1st/2nd year college students with programming or math interest (e.g. Arjun's profile).
steps.details: Leverage existing C language knowledge to build low-level security intuition. Weeks 1–3: C pointers in security, compiling with GCC on Linux, and Bandit 1–15. Weeks 4–6: Socket programming basics, network protocols, and Wireshark. Weeks 7–9: TryHackMe Pre-Security path + beginner crypto implementations (Caesar, XOR). Weeks 10–12: First public tool or detailed CTF writeup repository.

steps.title: Activate Pathway-Gamma: The IIT Research & Fast-Track
steps.description: For 2nd/3rd year engineering students aiming for C3iHub internships and 2027 entry (Debaprita's profile).
steps.details: Weeks 1–3: Advanced Linux administration, Docker containerization, and Python network automation. Weeks 4–6: Web application security (PortSwigger SQLi & XSS apprentices). Weeks 7–9: Building a functional security utility (e.g. packet sniffer or vulnerability scanner in Python). Weeks 10–12: Formal academic outreach dossier directed to C3iHub faculty.

steps.title: Set Your Non-Negotiable Milestone Rules
steps.description: Never move to the next block without finishing the current definition of done.
steps.details: A milestone is not 'I watched 5 videos'. A milestone is 'I ran the commands myself, solved the level, and wrote 5 lines of notes in my markdown file'. If you get stuck on a challenge for more than 45 minutes, look at a writeup, understand the conceptual failure, document it, and move forward.

steps.title: Master Linux Command Line with OverTheWire Bandit
steps.description: The gold standard for terminal muscle memory.
steps.details: Do not read an operating system book. Go straight to OverTheWire Bandit. Use SSH to connect. Levels 1 to 10 teach file permissions, piping, grep, base64 decoding, and hidden files. Levels 11 to 15 introduce SSL/TLS, port connection, and cron jobs. Benchmark: Reach Level 15 and write down the commands you learned.

steps.title: Learn Network Protocols with Wireshark & Sample PCAPs
steps.description: Inspect how data actually moves across wires.
steps.details: Download Wireshark. Download a free sample PCAP (Packet Capture) from Wireshark's sample wiki. Filter by 'http', 'dns', and 'tcp.flags.syn==1'. Observe the 3-way handshake in action. This hands-on visualization gives you 10x more intuition than memorizing OSI model layers from a textbook.

steps.title: Practice Web Security on PortSwigger Web Security Academy
steps.description: Created by the creators of Burp Suite — 100% free professional web security labs.
steps.details: Create a free account. Complete only the 'Apprentice' level labs for: (1) SQL Injection basics, and (2) Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) basics. Do not attempt Practitioner or Expert labs initially. Document the payload you used to solve each lab in your personal notes.

steps.title: Systems, Sockets, and C Programming References
steps.description: For candidates expanding into low-level systems (like Arjun).
steps.details: Consult 'Beej's Guide to Network Programming' — the internet's most accessible, legendary free guide to socket programming in C. Use CS50x lectures (Weeks 1 to 5) for clean memory models, pointers, and data structures.

steps.title: Structure Your Public GitHub Evidence Repository
steps.description: Create a clean, well-formatted repository documenting your learning journey.
steps.details: Name the repository 'cybersecurity-foundations' or 'iitk-bcyber-prep-journey'. Include a professional README.md with sections: (1) About My Motivation & Goals, (2) Hands-on Lab Log (Bandit, PortSwigger, PicoCTF), (3) Tools & Scripts Developed, (4) Key Technical Insights. A live GitHub profile with regular commits proves consistency.

steps.title: Document 2 Detailed CTF Challenge Writeups
steps.description: Show the committee how your brain works when solving problems.
steps.details: Pick two challenges you genuinely solved (e.g. 1 Bandit level and 1 PicoCTF crypto puzzle). Write a structured 1-page writeup for each: (1) Problem Statement, (2) Initial Hypotheses & Dead Ends, (3) The Breakthrough, (4) Final Solution & Key Takeaway. Faculty value cognitive clarity and persistence far more than rote answers.

steps.title: Develop 1 Mini-Script or Utility
steps.description: Build a simple, original utility in Python or C to prove practical capability.
steps.details: Ideas: A simple Python port scanner that checks open ports with socket module (30 lines); a Caesar/Vigenère cipher encrypter/decrypter with frequency analysis (50 lines); or a log parser that extracts failed login attempts from a sample auth.log file. Provide the source code and instructions to run it in your repository.

steps.title: The Optional 'Video Walkthrough' Edge
steps.description: How Ayush stood out from 1,000 flat PDF resumes.
steps.details: While not compulsory, a 2-minute screen recording provides an immense competitive advantage. Format: (0:00–0:25) Personal introduction, background, and what ignited your cybersecurity interest; (0:25–1:05) Screen recording of your terminal running your mini-tool or showing your Bandit notes; (1:05–1:40) One specific technical obstacle you failed at and how you figured it out; (1:40–2:00) Why IIT Kanpur's B.Cyber aligns with your long-term mission. Upload as Unlisted on YouTube and embed the link prominently in your PDF.

prompts.title: Video Walkthrough Scripting Framework
prompts.text: Draft a 150-word script for your 2-minute video following the 4-part structure: Hook & Passion -> Live Terminal Demo -> Problem-Solving Story -> IIT Kanpur Vision. Remove all buzzwords like 'I want to be an ethical hacker' and replace with concrete specifics like 'I spent three days understanding why my socket connection threw a timeout error.'

steps.title: The Hackathon Flag Triage Protocol
steps.description: How to score maximum points in a limited 3-to-4-hour laboratory hackathon.
steps.details: First 20 Minutes: Read every challenge title and description across all categories (Linux, Crypto, Web, Forensics). Categorize challenges into: Tier 1 (Obvious / Immediate flag extraction), Tier 2 (Clear path, requires 15 mins script/analysis), and Tier 3 (Complex / Cryptic). Rule: Solve all Tier 1 challenges in the first 45 minutes to secure a baseline score on the leaderboard before touching Tier 2 or 3.

steps.title: The 30-Minute Rabbit Hole Ejection Rule
steps.description: The exact trap that cost multiple candidates their selection.
steps.details: In an on-campus CTF, it is extraordinarily easy to spend 2 hours attempting to reverse-engineer a 100-point binary while three 50-point web/network flags sit untouched. Strict rule: If you make zero verifiable progress on a single challenge for 30 minutes, immediately close the tab, log your current state, and switch to a different category.

steps.title: The Exam-Week Emergency Protocol (60 Min/Week)
steps.description: What to do when JEE mock tests, pre-boards, or college semester exams hit.
steps.details: Do NOT feel guilty or quit the program. Shift into 'Sustain Mode': Drop your target to exactly 60 minutes on Sunday afternoon. Solve 1 single Bandit level or review 1 Wireshark capture. This preserves your neurological momentum and terminal familiarity without detracting from your academic exams.

steps.title: Recalibration Engine: Resetting When Life Changes
steps.description: Adjust your schedule dynamically when exam sessions end.
steps.details: Once a major exam finishes (e.g. JEE Main Session 1 or semester exams), run a Recalibration: Increase your weekly budget from 5 to 15 hours for a 2-week sprint. Review completed checklist items, re-sequence remaining milestones, and accelerate your proof-of-work assembly.
